mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.25% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 7.0% indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of months with UNRATE > 7.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) signal broad economic weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint decline in HOUST and PAYEMS fails to produce negative 20-day returns in >60% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing supply shock (INDPRO < 95.0) compresses profit margins and output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with INDPRO < 95.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.0% signals strong economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of quarters with GDPC1 growth >2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% signals monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates severe labor market contraction, reducing consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint rise in UNRATE and decline in PAYEMS fails to produce negative 5-day returns in >60% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0%) with accommodative policy (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) triggers anticipation of aggressive rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
